exception.reason: No main counterpart: main re-checked the admission gate inside the claim's write (hermes_state_runtime.py::claim_session_input runs _guard(conn) before its updates), while the backend's claim takes the gate as decided just before the write, and when a drain begins after that decision the claim's stamp callback (gateway/session_authority.py::SessionAuthority._claim_next) undoes the committed claim with this verb. Its fence reads refuse when a worker execution or a steering transfer is bound to the claim, and its two updates reverse the claim's two (the row back to queued with its queued owner epoch and no generation, runtime_generation back by one), so the ledger ends as main's refused claim leaves it, after a short window in which the claim is committed as started.

The verb takes the claim token (admission_id, generation) where main's gateway/session_settlement_recovery.py::_mark_unknown took the owner's row dict: the status update binds that admission_id, and the revision bump binds the target_session_id of the row the write re-reads, which is the caller's row target because only a queued row is ever re-targeted (hermes_state_runtime.py::rehome_queued_inputs) and this update runs only on a started row.

The verb takes the admission id and generation where main's gateway/session_results.py::finish_result read them from the owner's row dict (row['admission_id'], row['generation']); the result lookup binds RESULT_PREFIX + admission_id, the same key.

One partial-key lookup over the filters the caller gives (principal_id, target_session_id, request_id, admission_id), selecting whole rows in seq order and, with include_retired, appending the retired API tombstones of the request id through terminal_api_admissions, as main's gateway/platforms/api_server_response_admissions.py::_request_admission_rows did. Main's other gateway reads on (principal, request) in gateway/platforms/webhook_ingress.py::_committed, (target, request) in gateway/session_automation.py::_process_completed and in hermes_cli/kanban_owner_recovery.py::_admission_row (on the owner ledger the kanban receipt names, read through open_persistence_reader) and (principal 'api', request or admission id) in gateway/platforms/api_server_authority_runs.py::run_admission each projected their own columns; their callers now call this verb with those filters bound, and they are listed under not_moved.

The verb takes the status set and an optional principal: main's three SELECT DISTINCT target_session_id reads with literal values (status 'unknown' in gateway/run_runtime.py::release_unknown_turn_markers, statuses queued and unknown in gateway/run_runtime.py::recover_profile_native_sessions, principal 'api' with status queued in gateway/session_api_turn.py::recover_authority_api_turns) become one statement that binds the values their callers now pass. The other two are listed under not_moved.

The verb takes the target ids and the status set: main's probes for any queued or started row (gateway/run_idle_exit.py::_ledger_busy) and for any row on a session or its lineage owner (gateway/session_authorities.py::holds_admission) become one SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1 that binds the values their callers now pass. The second is listed under not_moved.

Main's gateway/platforms/api_server_response_store.py::ResponseStore._settle_terminal_admissions read state.db on a read-only connection of its own (sqlite3's default 5 s lock wait), outside any store transaction, running the two chunked statements over the ids its own table held. The verb runs the same statements over the ids the caller passes in one read context of the read-only handle the caller opens (persistence_assembly.py::open_persistence_reader), whose connection waits 5 s on a lock as main's did.

The candidate predicate is the module constant _CANDIDATES, the same text main built as a local string in gateway/session_api_media.py::compact_settled_api_payloads, and the checker compares the name, not its value; the rewrite between the re-read and the UPDATE is session_rules/api_payloads.py::compacted_api_payload, main's _compacted and history drop moved into a rule module, run inside the same write as main ran it.

One verb reads the candidates of either kind: main's two primary-key range reads in hermes_state_media.py::collect_retired_spillover and hermes_state_media.py::collect_retired_media differ only in the bound prefix range, which the verb picks from its kind parameter (SPILLOVER_PREFIX or PREFIX). The media read is listed under not_moved.

One verb deletes collected keys of either kind: main's two DELETE statements bound the keys its collectors computed in the same function, and the verb binds the keys the caller passes (session_retention.py::collect_retired_spillover and session_retention.py::collect_retired_media compute them as main did), in one write per call as main's were. The media delete is listed under not_moved.

Main's hermes_state_runtime.py::_epoch is also reached from the hosted-room import's write (gateway/hosted_rooms_gateway_import.py::import_standalone_rooms, an immediate transaction on the gateway's state.db); the backend serves that fence with its own copy persistence/sqlite/gateway/_hosted_rooms_common.py::_epoch inside persistence/sqlite/gateway/hosted_rooms.py::SQLiteHostedRoomRepository.import_fenced_rooms, so this copy keeps only the runtime, admission and transcript callers' labels.
